approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from an unlabeled corpus, then starts a fresh policy for each objective. After each accepted batch it trains on the current best-scoring half plus a uniform sample of older elites from a memory of the thirty-two highest-scoring accepted identities. It preserves each molecule's original accepted SMILES and score. The policy log probability for each training sequence is fitted toward that sequence's frozen prior log probability plus sixty times its observed reward, with equal row weights. Novel molecules are then sampled directly from the adapted policy and checked for chemical validity and canonical duplicates.
approach.novelty: Replay a historical molecule through an equivalent SMILES traversal instead of always repeating its original string. The same accepted molecule and score remain the training example, while the traversal changes which token contexts carry that feedback. Current elites still use their original strings, and memory membership and sampling stay intact. This tests a different route to transfer from the siblings that changed replay selection or core retention. It also differs from alternative-string prior preparation: the prior stays unchanged, and views receive only the historical molecule's actual accepted reward during online adaptation. One deterministic equivalent view is reserved from training for each molecule so that transfer can be checked beyond the strings fitted.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-15499bde2e65 repeatedly fits each historical molecule only through its exact accepted serialization. Historical replay already contributes gradients, but those receipts establish neither equivalent-sequence transfer nor useful chemical generalization. A read-only audit enumerating deterministic atom-rooted equivalent SMILES for the actual historical records in all three Parent seeds found verified changed training strings and a separate held-out equivalent string for every one of 2100 nonterminal replay exposures in 420 updates. A deterministic per-identity/per-feedback-batch choice would use 2014 distinct training strings, with no held-out string used for training. Training pools contain 7 to 52 distinct alternatives after holding out one view. All audited views preserve canonical/isomeric identity and the inherited token-length bound; only unchanged root spellings were rejected. Sibling n-06c043e9d303 enriches replay scores but concentrates output, while n-b8abee8a6172 broadens retained cores and reduces duplicates with only +0.000922 mean final-score change. Both still fit original strings. Sibling n-496abfe104f6 shows that unlabeled prior view exposure can improve alternative likelihood while worsening original likelihood and validity; it does not test score-conditioned historical-view transfer with the prior held unchanged.
hypothesis: Replace the original serialization of each uniformly selected historical elite with a deterministic accepted-identity-equivalent atom-rooted SMILES training view, preserving its original accepted record and score, while reserving one distinct equivalent view from training and keeping current elites, memory membership, the frozen prior and the inherited online loss unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Equivalent replay improves unseen spellings while weakening original support and final scores
finding_summary.insights: The new spellings entered the loss and transferred some fitting benefit to excluded spellings, so absence of exposure or complete failure of sequence transfer cannot explain the score loss. That transfer came with weaker support for the originally accepted strings, rather than better fitting across all representations. Keeping the prior fixed did not prevent this tradeoff. The original reward is preserved, but the inherited target depends on the spelling: the new views lower its value by about 47.86 log-likelihood units on average, and reduce positive, unattainable targets from 461 to 64 on the same accepted examples. Thus improved view fit combines different token contexts with different numeric targets; it does not establish representation-independent reward learning. Fewer duplicate samples and somewhat broader core coverage also fail to establish useful molecular transfer. The generated molecules still include recognizable carbonyl and cyclic-amine families, but changed leading arrangements do not consistently improve objectives, and the chemistry assessment retains stereochemical and reactive-group gaps. The experiment confirms a working view-replay and held-out-transfer mechanism while rejecting its overall utility under this panel.
finding_summary.results: All 2100 historical replay exposures before subsequent sampling used verified new spellings of the same accepted molecules. Their gradients differed measurably from original-string replay in all 420 eligible updates. Reserved equivalent strings, never used for training, improved their mean squared target error from 202.59 to 169.07; every task and seed showed this improvement. However, original historical strings worsened from 144.14 to 152.33, and their average likelihood fell in every session. Duplicate draws dropped from 30.11% to 14.07%, but raw chemical validity fell from 90.43% to 87.24%. The three-seed macro mean declined from 0.507554 to 0.493167, a paired loss of 0.014387 against the required gain of 0.002. Deco_hop improved in all seeds; sitagliptin declined in all seeds.

molecular.headline: Conventional amide and cyclic-amine families coexist with polyfluorinated amidoximes, polynitro aromatics and incomplete stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five tasks have complete supplied trajectories for three seeds, with 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. The dominant chemistry is ring-rich and recognizable: aryl/heteroaryl amides, pyrazole carboxamides, sulfonamides, cyclic amines, hydrazone or azine connections, and heteroaromatic carbonyl systems. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 23, 26, 26, 23 and 24 in fixed task order; median ring count is three throughout. Digest aromatic-token rates are 0.9437-0.9920 and ring-closure rates 0.9747-0.9966. The main limitations are therefore not absent rings or aromatic atoms. There are 460-762 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds per task, but leading molecules concentrate in several local chemical families. Most connectivity is synthetically plausible, with specific qualification for repeated nitro substitution, amidoxime/hydrazone geometry, occasional isocyanides and chloroalkyl appendages. In the most nitro-rich session, the digest charged rate of 0.2586 includes nitro and other internally charge-separated groups: 216 proposals contain nitro groups, but only five have nonzero net formal charge. Relative to the parent, familiar carbonyl and cyclic-amine chemistry persists, while different positional arrangements and nitrogen-linker families dominate individual high-score sets. No proposal contains assigned stereocentres; 184, 62, 414, 231 and 308 proposals contain an unassigned centre in task order. These structural observations do not establish synthesis, physical properties, stability or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: The two highest molecules are compact alpha-aryl, alpha-pyridyl acetamides with an N-pyridyl amide substituent. They have three aromatic six-membered rings, 23 or 24 heavy atoms and an unassigned central stereocentre. Another family is an N-aryl pyrazole carboxamide, while much of the remaining leading digest consists of azine-linked thiazolidinone-like carbonyl rings carrying two haloaryl regions. Those latter examples contain a C=N-N=C connection whose configuration is not specified. The parent led with substituted indole carboxamides; the current highest family rearranges its aromatic and carbonyl groups around a stereogenic acyclic carbon instead. N-N=C proposals number 101 versus 34 in the parent, consistent with the greater visibility of nitrogen-linked imine chemistry in the current output.
liabilities: C=N-N=C and related imine connections introduce E/Z and tautomeric questions not resolved by the displayed scores.
Several equal-score haloaryl variants increase mass without demonstrating a benefit in the visible gradient.
Four proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and bulky multiply linked structures dominate the very low-score tail despite familiar individual functional groups.
missing_features: The highest acetamides do not specify their stereogenic central carbon, so the useful three-ring/polar arrangement has not been proposed as distinct configurations.

The leading region has limited chemically distinct alternatives beyond acetamide, pyrazole and azine-linked analogue families; repeated halogen substitutions do not address the missing precise placement of polar groups.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methylphenyl/pyridyl acetamide scores 0.454082 and the methoxyphenyl counterpart 0.453163. In the latter framework, replacing the alpha-pyridyl ring with phenyl gives 0.375059 in the terminal digest, supporting the value of that ring-nitrogen placement within this local arrangement. The pyrazole carboxamide reaches 0.436818. Numerous halo-substitution variants of the azine/thiazolidinone family all score 0.413359, so their extra chlorine or fluorine changes do not establish a useful gradient. By contrast, very large peptide-like, polycyclic or extended aromatic assemblies are as low as approximately 2.93e-67, while a simple arylsulfonamide terminal molecule is about 3.66e-08. The useful association is organized moderate-size aromatic/carbonyl chemistry, not either maximal size or an isolated polar group.

per_task.generated_character: The highest structure is a compact hydroxy aza-fused aromatic sulfonamide bearing a difluoroanilino group: 24 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 353.310. Other leaders include polyfluorinated aryl amidines, amidoximes and aminoheteroaryl systems. One high example is an isocyanide-bearing multi-heteroaryl molecule, and another has four nitro groups across an aromatic ether assembly. The whole proposal set has median 26 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and a very low median sp3-carbon fraction of about 0.0833. There are 216 nitro-containing proposals and 102 O-N=C matches, the latter reflecting abundant oxime/amidoxime chemistry. Parent leaders included aromatic acylhydrazones and fluorinated heteroaryl systems; current N-N=C proposals fall from 181 to eight while the displayed imine chemistry shifts toward amidines and amidoximes. These motifs are synthetically recognizable, but repeated nitro and fluorine decoration narrows their apparent medicinal-chemistry quality.
liabilities: Polynitro aromatic systems and the isocyanide example introduce reactivity or stability questions that differ from ordinary amides and sulfonamides; valid graph representations do not resolve them.
The charged-string rate should not be interpreted as a population of ionic molecules: only five proposals have nonzero net formal charge, while 216 contain nitro groups.
Strong aromatic bias and extensive aryl fluorination provide little saturated shape in many leaders, and seven proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
missing_features: The leading output lacks broad stable alternatives that reproduce the useful polar/aromatic arrangement without relying so heavily on dense fluorination, amidoxime variants or repeated nitro substitution.
Amidine and amidoxime C=N configurations are unspecified, and their tautomeric or ionization behavior is not established by the supplied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact difluoroanilino sulfonamide scores 0.612372, a more heavily fluorinated aryl amidine 0.606725 and an aminoheteroaryl compound 0.606682. These show that maximal fluorination or aromatic expansion is not necessary for the highest displayed score. Within a specific amidoxime pair, a more fluorinated aryl region scores 0.602841 versus 0.571754 for its less fluorinated terminal counterpart, supporting a local substituent effect without a universal fluorine rule. The polynitro aromatic ether scores 0.598691 and the isocyanide-bearing example 0.604700, so these liabilities are tolerated. Low-score benzyl, alkyl or cyclic sulfones lie near 0.262-0.302 despite sulfur, oxygen and aromatic rings; their different attachment context matters.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule joins an amino-oxazole-like aromatic ring to a substituted cyclohexane, an ethyl linker and an arylpiperazine. It has 27 heavy atoms, four rings, two aromatic rings and molecular mass 372.488, with unspecified stereochemistry in the substituted saturated ring. Most other leaders are arylpiperazines or seven-membered diazepanes linked to diarylmethyl or aryl/cyclohexyl regions, often bearing bromine or multiple chlorines. These are recognizable basic-amine medicinal-chemistry families. Parent leaders also had arylpiperazine and fused-amine architectures, including indole-linked examples; the current leading neighborhood emphasizes saturated cyclohexyl and diarylalkyl arms. Full proposals have median 26 heavy atoms and three rings, but their median score is only 0.027500: the near-ceiling structures do not describe the typical score or all of the generated chemistry.
liabilities: Diarylmethyl arms, long linkers and multiple bromine or chlorine substituents raise mass and conformational freedom without demonstrating a general need in the highest structure.
Several leaders approach or exceed molecular mass 500, while the highest displayed molecule is 372.488.
Eleven proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms and the largest has 88, so otherwise familiar amine chemistry can expand into much less economical whole molecules.
missing_features: The output already reaches useful cyclic-amine arrangements, but those arrangements are inadequately represented across a population whose median score remains 0.027500.

Relative configuration on the substituted cyclohexane and configuration at diaryl/aryl-cyclohexyl centres are unspecified; 414 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre and no proposal assigns one.
No additional required pharmacophoric group can be inferred from the near-ceiling examples; precise alternative arrangements are better supported than prescribed extra substituents.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoheteroaryl/cyclohexyl piperazine scores 0.999994 and a diarylalkyl diazepane 0.999984. Haloaryl piperazine analogues lie around 0.99, indicating that a basic ring nitrogen positioned between aromatic and saturated hydrophobic regions is productive across several topologies. The top molecule does not require the extensive heavy-halogen decoration of many nearby leaders. Low examples are rich in amide, sulfonamide, nitro or hydrazone functionality, approximately 3.80e-05 to 6.08e-05, with different nitrogen electronics and spatial arrangements. This supports contextual amine presentation rather than nitrogen or ring counts alone. The comparison describes supplied molecular scores and does not establish receptor activity or a universal ring-amine requirement.

per_task.generated_character: Leading molecules include arylsulfonylpiperazines, methylenedioxybenzyl piperazines and fused lactam/indole structures. The highest example is a piperazine bearing an ethoxy/methoxy arylsulfonyl group and a bis-amide side chain, with 33 heavy atoms, three rings and molecular mass 479.530. A much simpler methylphenylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine has only 17 heavy atoms and two rings. A methylenedioxybenzyl N-methylpiperazine also has 17 heavy atoms. These are plausible conventional chemotypes. The parent already had a simple N-methyl arylsulfonylpiperazine and fused carbonyl alternatives among its leaders, so the principal chemistry is shared while the attachment patterns vary. Full proposals have median 23 heavy atoms and three rings, with 736 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Acylated and sulfonylated piperazine nitrogens are electronically different from free tertiary amines; the leading family cannot be summarized as simply adding more basic centres.
Large bis-amide or fused-ring appendages increase synthetic and physical-property burdens while remaining close in score to compact examples.
Five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and exceptionally long alkyl chains appear at the low end of the observed distribution.
missing_features: The leading repertoire needs more precise alternatives in aromatic/piperazine attachment and polar-linker placement; larger elaborations provide little visible separation from simple structures.
Configuration remains unspecified in chiral fused carbonyl alternatives and in 231 proposals overall, although the simplest piperazines are achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The larger bis-amide/sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.208126, the simple arylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine 0.207671 and the methylenedioxybenzyl N-methylpiperazine 0.204569. Their close scores show that the added aromatic ring, amides and size of the largest example are not clearly necessary. These structures associate organized aromatic, cyclic-nitrogen and polar-linker regions with the higher visible scores, but not a unique ionization pattern: the highest piperazine has both nitrogens sulfonylated or acylated, unlike the basic N-methyl alternatives. Small polar species or simple cycloalkyl amines score approximately 0.008-0.029, and very long-chain molecules remain near 0.018-0.020. Adding polarity, basic nitrogen or size alone therefore does not reproduce the useful arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a tert-butyl-substituted nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic carbonyl ring attached to a benzamide with a 2-chloroethyl substituent: 23 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. Other leaders include a benzimidazole/pyrazole-like heteroaryl system bearing an ethyl methylsulfone side chain, a trimethoxyaryl pyridyl acylhydrazone, compact aminoheteroaromatics and nitroaryl thiosemicarbazone-like structures. These are mostly recognizable synthetic families, with specific concerns for the chloroethyl arm, imine geometry and sulfur/nitrogen-chain chemistry. Parent leaders also included fused nitrogen/carbonyl structures and compact polar amides, but the current digest supplies different combinations and sparse moderate-score examples. Full proposals have median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with 762 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. The worst displayed molecules include oversized peptide-like, polyfunctional or heavily chlorinated multiaryl assemblies.
liabilities: The primary chloroethyl arm is a possible electrophilic side-chain liability, while nitroaryl and thiosemicarbazone-like examples introduce separate reactivity or stability questions.
Large peptide-like and heavily elaborated aromatic structures can contain many familiar polar groups while giving exactly zero score; eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
Terminal sulfur/disulfide or highly substituted fused structures add chemistry whose practical stability and physical properties are not established by the trajectories.
missing_features: More precise and broader coverage of compact polar heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements is missing even though several viable-looking families are already produced.
Stable alternatives to the chloroethyl and thiosemicarbazone-like features are not demonstrated as matched high-score analogues; the visible data do not establish those liabilities as required.
Hydrazone C=N geometry is unspecified, and no proposal assigns stereocentres despite 308 containing an unassigned centre; many of the displayed leaders themselves are achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzamide/heteroaromatic-carbonyl molecule scores 0.268815, the sulfone-substituted heteroaryl molecule 0.233604 and the trimethoxyaryl acylhydrazone 0.229727. Compact aminoheteroaromatic and sulfur-containing alternatives reach roughly 0.18-0.23. Those examples suggest a preference for particular compact polar arrangements without establishing any one mandatory group; the highest chloroethyl substituent is not shown in a matched pair proving its necessity. The large peptide-like and multiaryl molecules are zero or vanishing. The digest median is rounded to 0.0: the full 900-row median is 1.766839397052908e-07 and seven rows are exactly zero. Thus the higher-score chemistry occupies a sparse part of a predominantly very-low-score population, not a population of literal zeros.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A methoxyphenyl/pyridyl acetamide scores 0.453163 while its displayed phenyl-for-pyridyl counterpart scores 0.375059. In another set, conventional cyclic-amine leaders reach near-ceiling scores while typical output has a median of 0.027500 and low examples place nitrogen in amides, sulfonamides or hydrazones. A further leading set includes both a piperazine with acylated/sulfonylated nitrogens and basic N-methylpiperazines at nearly equal scores, showing that useful nitrogen chemistry depends on the surrounding arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently reproduce the precise placement and electronic context of useful polar groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support meaningful alternatives in ring-nitrogen position, amide orientation and linker attachment while preserving the useful structural relationships suggested by feedback. Treat free amines, amide nitrogens, sulfonamide nitrogens, amidines and hydrazones as distinct chemical environments rather than interchangeable nitrogen content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per-session nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts range from 460 to 762, yet digest leaders repeat acetamide, azine/thiazolidinone, fluorinated amidoxime or cyclic-amine families. Several haloaryl azine variants have the same score of 0.413359. One structurally diverse session has 762 scaffolds but a full-trajectory median score near 1.77e-07. Meanwhile, 33- and 17-heavy-atom piperazine structures in another session score 0.208126 and 0.207671, illustrating that added size is not necessarily useful coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold counts do not provide sufficiently broad coverage of productive, economical chemical families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically distinct core and linker alternatives that preserve an observed useful arrangement, alongside controlled local variation. Measure chemical breadth through access to productive families and alternatives, rather than more unique graphs, repetitive halogen changes or larger appendages alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 184, 62, 414, 231 and 308 proposals with unassigned centres. Higher-score examples include alpha-aryl/heteroaryl acetamides, substituted cyclohexyl cyclic amines, diarylalkyl centres and fused lactams. Amidoxime, hydrazone and azine leaders also omit explicit C=N configuration; one session contains 102 O-N=C matches.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereogenic centres and configurationally variable nitrogen double bonds unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable chemically consistent, explicitly configured alternatives when a proposed structure has stereocentres or relevant imine geometry, while retaining achiral chemistry. The supplied observations do not identify a preferred unobserved stereoisomer or tautomer, so those possibilities must remain empirically distinguishable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One session contains 216 nitro-bearing proposals and displays a four-nitro aromatic ether at 0.598691, while its highest structure is a smaller difluoroanilino sulfonamide at 0.612372. An isocyanide and dense fluorinated amidoximes also appear among leaders. Elsewhere, the highest compact benzamide carries a primary chloroethyl arm without a matched example proving that arm necessary. Across sessions, four, seven, eleven, five and eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and long-chain or peptide-like structures recur among very low or zero scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator needs stable and less burdensome alternatives to repeated reactive-group decoration and excessive molecular growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain access to conventional stable linkers and substituents that realize useful polar arrangements with controlled mass and appendage size. Distinguish potentially reactive nitro-rich, isocyanide, imine-chain and haloalkyl motifs from ordinary aromatic substitution, and avoid treating tolerated chemical burden as evidence that more of it is required.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
